content: 1. Information regarding the timing of different supplements, whether taken simultaneously or at different times of the day, should be meticulously recorded. This includes an evaluation of the feasibility and acceptability of taking multiple supplements at varying times during clinical trials. 2. The updated global guideline will be made available online for download and as a printed publication. Printed versions will be distributed to WHO regional and country offices, ministries of health, WHO collaborating centers, and non-governmental organization partners, using the same distribution list developed for the WHO ANC guideline. 3. The updated recommendations and derivative products, such as the WHO Antenatal Care Recommendations Adaptation Toolkit and its instruction manual, will be disseminated during meetings and scientific conferences attended by WHO staff. Social media channels will also be utilized for dissemination. 4. The executive summary and recommendations from this publication will be translated into the six United Nations languages and disseminated through WHO regional offices and during meetings organized or attended by WHO staff. 5. This updated recommendation supersedes the WHO ANC guideline recommendation on zinc supplementation issued in 2016 (Recommendation A6). The Guideline Development Group (GDG) agreed that there were no new implementation considerations or applicability issues specific to this recommendation, as it was recommended in a research context. 6. Monitoring of the uptake and impact of this updated recommendation will be integrated into the monitoring framework of the 2016 WHO ANC guideline. For implementation considerations related to WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience, refer to the guideline and associated derivative products available on WHO websites. 7. Research is needed to evaluate the interactions among nutrients such as iron and calcium, which are often provided as part of routine antenatal care, in relation to maternal and newborn outcomes. This is particularly important in settings where iron supplementation is universally recommended and calcium supplementation is advised in areas with low dietary intake. 8. Trials on zinc supplementation in settings providing iron and folic acid as part of routine antenatal care should include various doses of zinc along with 30 mg and/or 60 mg of elemental iron, in accordance with national guidance. Detailed information on the timing of supplement intake, whether taken together or separately, should be recorded, along with an assessment of the feasibility and acceptability of taking multiple supplements at different times. 9. WHO convenes the Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG) biannually to review its portfolio of maternal and perinatal health recommendations and to advise on the prioritization of new and existing questions for recommendation development and updating. 10. WHO will monitor the publication of new randomized trials on this topic. Any concerns about the validity of the recommendation will be promptly communicated via the guideline website, and plans will be made to update the recommendation as necessary. 11. WHO will prioritize its independent normative guidance, informed by the strategic shifts embedded in its Constitution and the Thirteenth General Programme of Work (2019–2023). 12. All technical products developed during the process of creating this recommendation, including the Cochrane RevMan file customized for priority outcomes and the basis for quality ratings within the GRADE process, will be archived in the departmental shared folder for future reference and use.
